solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Loud organ causing fright

parts.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
the organ of hearing

explanation.surface: Someone hears a booming church organ and is startled by it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loud organ' reads as a pipe organ, but it splits into a musical abbreviation and a body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Both nouns name the sudden alarm felt when something scares a person.

clue.text: Father with lawsuit getting tiny amount

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
an action is a case brought in court

explanation.surface: A man sues someone and wins only a pitiful payout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' simply attaches the second piece to the first.
explanation.definitionFit: A small part or portion of a whole, as in 'a fraction of the cost', is a synonym for a little bit.

clue.text: Influential part abandoned by fine thespian

indicators.note: when something is abandoned by a companion, that companion departs, so a letter leaves the word

parts.note: a factor is an element that influences an outcome
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: A once-influential role is dropped by a good performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Influential part' sounds like a stage role, which fits 'thespian', but it means a contributing element.
explanation.definitionFit: A thespian is a stage performer, from Thespis, the legendary first Greek player of drama.

clue.text: Mostly deal with certain valuable objects

indicators.note: most but not all of something means its final letter is cut off

parts.note: to treat is to deal with, here shorn of its last letter
sure means certain

explanation.surface: Mostly dealing with certain precious items, like an antiques trader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal with' looks like one phrase for the first piece, but only 'deal' is used; 'with' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure is a collective noun for precious items such as gold, jewels and other riches.

clue.text: Narcotic product extracted from tree ferns

indicators.note: something extracted is drawn out of what holds it, so the letters lie inside the following words

parts.note: running across the two words

explanation.surface: A drug produced by processing plants of the fern family.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a plant-derived drug, which neatly matches the answer's sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A reefer is slang for a cannabis cigarette, a drug product rolled for smoking.

clue.text: Possible application for program meeting?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a job or post that one might apply for
second meaning: a meeting scheduled in advance

explanation.surface: Wondering whether some software app could arrange meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'application' and 'program' pull towards computer software; instead one is a job application and the other a verb, to schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both a post someone is given after applying and an arranged time to meet someone.

clue.text: At college just standing

parts.note: to be up is to be in residence at university
just in the sense of fair or correct

explanation.surface: Someone at college has only just got to their feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' looks like 'only' or 'recently', but here means fair. Being 'up' at Oxford or Cambridge is British usage for studying there.
explanation.definitionFit: Upright describes something vertical or on its feet, a direct synonym for erect.

clue.text: Day before getting new flat

parts.note: the eve is the day before an event
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Someone collects the keys to their new flat the day before moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' reads as a British apartment, but it is an adjective meaning level.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe a level, smooth surface without bumps or slopes.

clue.text: Case for an embassy worker

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a slim briefcase for documents, short for the full name of that case
second meaning: a diplomatic staff member with a specialist role

explanation.surface: A briefcase meant for someone on an ambassador's staff.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hides that the briefcase is literally named after the diplomat who might carry it.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word names a junior diplomatic official, and the hard document case is called after such officials.

clue.text: Secret family group to ordain

parts.note: a clan is an extended family group
to destine is to ordain or foreordain

explanation.surface: A hidden family society plans to consecrate one of its members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordain' suggests making someone a priest, but here it means to decree or predetermine.
explanation.definitionFit: Both adjectives describe something done covertly, kept hidden from others.

clue.text: Quiet compulsion to get out

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for quiet
an urge is a strong compulsion

explanation.surface: A silent, nagging wish to escape somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get out' sounds like leaving, but it means expelling or ridding something.
explanation.definitionFit: To purge is to rid oneself of something, expelling or clearing it away entirely.

clue.text: No good chasing Henrietta — terribly scary

indicators.note: one who chases runs behind the quarry, so this piece is placed after the other
doing something terribly means doing it badly, so these letters come out in a mangled order

parts.note: the name taken as written
NG is the abbreviation for no good

explanation.surface: A useless suitor pursues a woman called Henrietta in a frightening way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chasing' means following, so the abbreviation goes after the rearranged name.
explanation.definitionFit: Something menacing that promises harm is frightening, so the two adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Clergyman beginning on rite always with purpose

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the opening letter of the word
ever means always
an end is an aim or purpose

explanation.surface: A priest begins a ritual, always acting with intent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'purpose' as 'end' is the sense in 'to that end'.
explanation.definitionFit: The title is the honorific used for ordained ministers, and by extension names a priest or vicar.

clue.text: Working with team in agreement

parts.note: a machine that is working is on
a side is a sports team

explanation.surface: Cooperating with colleagues who all agree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'team' as 'side' is the sporting sense, as in a football side.
explanation.definitionFit: To be onside is idiomatic for being supportive of a plan or person, like agreeing with them.

clue.text: Weapon can be expensive to acquire in video game

indicators.note: one thing placed in another sits inside it, surrounded on both sides

parts.note: a sim is a simulation video game
dear means costly to buy

explanation.surface: A gamer complains that buying a gun in the game costs too much.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about in-game purchases, so 'in video game' looks like scene-setting, not an instruction to insert.
explanation.definitionFit: A sidearm is a pistol or other small firearm carried at the hip, one kind of weapon.

clue.text: Model university in New York, say

indicators.note: something sitting in a place is held within it

parts.note: New York is an example of a US state; 'say' flags the example
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: Praising an exemplary university in New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' reads as an adjective meaning exemplary, but it is a noun: a sculpted figure. New York, say, is the state, not the city.
explanation.definitionFit: A sculpted figure representing a person is a three-dimensional likeness, much like a model.

clue.text: Desire what church will often support

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to long or aim for something

definitions.note: read as two words, an article and a noun
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a tall pointed tower that rises from many church roofs, with the article in front

explanation.surface: Wishing for what a congregation usually backs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'support' looks like backing a cause, but it is physical: a church building holds up a tall tower.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspire is to set one's hopes on achieving something, the verb sense of wanting.

clue.text: Break up when taking part in masquerade

indicators.note: a participant goes inside the activity, so one piece is set within another

parts.note: to dissemble is to disguise one's true nature
as means when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Splitting up a couple at a costume ball.
explanation.walkthrough: 'masquerade' looks like a noun for a ball, but here it is a verb meaning to pretend.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something apart into its components is to break it up into pieces.

clue.text: Book career for cleaner

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for book
to career is to rush along headlong

explanation.surface: Reserving a job as a cleaner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' looks like a noun meaning profession, but it is a verb meaning to hurtle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bristled tool used for sweeping or scrubbing is something that cleans.

clue.text: Go round abolishing king in comedy sketch

indicators.note: to abolish is to do away with, so a letter is taken out

parts.note: to skirt is to go round something
R is rex, Latin for king; this letter is removed

explanation.surface: A satirical sketch that goes round getting rid of the monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go round' means to bypass the edge of something.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a short humorous piece of theatre, the same thing as a brief funny sketch.

clue.text: Fabric ending up pink peach taffeta, dark one

indicators.note: the ending of each word is its final letter, which is all that is kept

parts.note: the final letter of each of the four words
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A dress made of pink and peach taffeta ends up in a dark version.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' is not a final-letter source; it is the Roman numeral added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Khaki is a sturdy dull-brownish cloth, originally used for military uniforms.

clue.text: Meddle with untried arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement puts things into a new order, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tinkering with a new, untested plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meddle with' looks like a phrasal verb, but 'with' is just the link.
explanation.definitionFit: To meddle is to interfere in others' affairs uninvited, which is to butt in.

clue.text: Like a tuned piano worked some of the time swallowing note

indicators.note: whatever swallows something takes it inside itself

parts.note: to temp is to work as a temporary, only part of the time
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A piano tuner who works part time finds one note gets swallowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some of the time' is not a hidden-word signal but describes temping. A piano is tuned to equal temperament.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, a keyboard tuned so intervals are adjusted to suit all keys is said to be in equal temperament.

clue.text: Drop building on garden plot, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to cast off, as a tree does leaves
second meaning: a simple hut for tools

explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals that the garden plot is only one place such a hut might stand.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to cast off or let fall, and the noun is a small wooden outbuilding for storage.
